unit: fleet regression: stall-speed, minimum-drag-speed, minimum-sink-speed, stall-break, parabolic-polar-fit through compute()
text: At least the aircraft with published measurements are compared with those measurements (stall of the Avistar Elite ~12 m/s, FASER data).
note: reference/avistar_elite/MEASUREMENTS.md: 'Nothing here is used by a test'. The only non-self values are three numbers of the CRRCSim prototype, computed with the same AeroSandbox.

unit: fleet regression: stall-speed, minimum-drag-speed, minimum-sink-speed, stall-break, parabolic-polar-fit through compute()
text: V_S < V_mp < V_md for every aircraft that computes (physics of a polar).
note: V_mp < V_md asserted for the six MVP aircraft only; V_S < V_mp nowhere; none for the 28 plan models (their recorded goldens do satisfy it, checked by script).

unit: fleet regression: stall-speed, minimum-drag-speed, minimum-sink-speed, stall-break, parabolic-polar-fit through compute()
text: V_S = sqrt(2 m g / (rho S C_L,max)) links the three recorded outputs; V_S grows with sqrt(m) at equal C_L,max.
note: The goldens are mutually consistent (checked by script to 2e-3) but no test asserts the relation or a mass variation.

unit: fleet regression: stall-speed, minimum-drag-speed, minimum-sink-speed, stall-break, parabolic-polar-fit through compute()
text: A golden holds for named tool versions; a different version is noticed at the assert, not as drifting numbers.
note: test_stall_speed_fleet compares provenance with the installed version (self-comparison), not with 4.2.9 / 0.3.2; the chain, plan-batch, neutral-point and roll files pin no version at all.

unit: fleet regression: neutral-point, static margin, design CG, tail arms
text: For a conventional tail the neutral point lies aft of the wing's quarter-chord point and ahead of the tail.
note: Only one test brackets x_NP (0.10 < x < 0.17 m for BRYAN with NACA 2412); no relation to the wing's quarter chord for the fleet.

unit: fleet regression: neutral-point, static margin, design CG, tail arms
text: A flying wing has a neutral point (or a declared unsupported_layout).
note: VOODOO and WINDFREAK pin the error code unsupported_layout as their golden; the tailless chain is not computed anywhere.

unit: fleet regression: lateral MVP chain (tail volumes, spiral, turn sideslip, rudder roll authority) and the plan batch
text: A positive spiral criterion is a stable spiral reported as a negative (halving) time with the warning spiral_halving_time_reported; a negative criterion gives a positive doubling time.
note: Three aircraft at the md point; the same sign relation holds in all recorded plan-batch goldens (checked by script) but is not asserted for them.

unit: fleet regression: lateral MVP chain (tail volumes, spiral, turn sideslip, rudder roll authority) and the plan batch
text: No fleet aircraft ends in an error of category internal (ARCHITECTURE 8.1: internal is a defect).
note: MINI_FUNTANA's 13 lateral quantities are pinned as Failed('internal') (bug #1373): the suite is green while the defect exists and nothing stops a second internal error from being recorded the same way.

unit: fleet regression: lateral MVP chain (tail volumes, spiral, turn sideslip, rudder roll authority) and the plan batch
text: A broken chain (binding between formulas on real fleet geometry) is noticed by the PR tier, which excludes aero.
note: No unmarked test runs the MVP chain on a fleet aircraft through compute() with stubbed solvers; aero runs only with the ci-full label or nightly (.github/workflows/test.yml).

unit: fleet regression: lateral MVP chain (tail volumes, spiral, turn sideslip, rudder roll authority) and the plan batch
text: Re-recording goldens is a reviewed act: a tool writes them and reports old/new, so a regression cannot be blessed unnoticed.
note: No recorder script, no update flag, no diff report; the MVP files keep hand-written 'was' comments, the 812 plan-batch cells keep none.

text: No quantity, a duplicate quantity or a malformed aircraft reference answers 422 with the envelope code validation_error.
note: The three malformed-reference cases assert the status code only.

text: Physically inadmissible input (mass <= 0, Q8) reaches the client as input_errors with input_path and empty quantities; one shape of 'invalid input' for the client.
note: Only with a stubbed kernel at service level. The real validation is never run through the endpoint; parse failures answer 422 with dict items, kernel validation 200 with KernelError objects, and no test states that this split is intended.

text: A failure inside the kernel that is not a ServiceException still answers with the one error envelope (ADR 0019), without internal paths.
note: The service test proves the exception propagates; at the endpoint it becomes Starlette's plain-text 'Internal Server Error' (measured), and no test covers it.

text: needs_confirmation lists exactly the requested quantities skipped with reason long_run_not_included.
note: No quantity skipped for another reason in the test: dropping the reason-code filter survives (P8-M04).

text: Every cached compute runs on one kernel loop that is not the caller's; a failure reaches the caller; a caller that leaves does not break the loop; shutdown closes the kernel on that loop.
note: The guard for a cancelled caller in _settle can be removed without a failing test (P8-M15).

text: All dimensional spar fields (width, height, length, start, origin, section) are converted from millimetres to metres; spare_vector is not scaled.
note: The canon test asserts width, height, start and the vector; length and origin are killed only by app/tests/test_wing_service_extended.py through the shared function (P8-M10, M11); section by test_spar_section_gh1428.py.

unit: app/services/assumption_compute_service.py (stall-speed binding of the legacy app computation)
text: C_L,max that sizes V_S is the C_L,max at V_S (fixed point within 2 %).
note: The docstring says the test is expected to fail (gh-1142); it carries no xfail and runs only in the nightly slow tier. State not verified (not run). The kernel's own stall solve has no such fixed-point test in this package.

text: IPOPT minimises V (not drag, not lift) on the pre-stall branch.
note: Fast tier: FakeOpti.minimize is a no-op (probe P6a-M01b survived); only the real solver pins the objective.

text: The constraint is L(V, alpha) = n m g.
note: Fast tier: FakeOpti.subject_to is a no-op (P6a-M02 survived); pinned by the aero probe to 1e-6 against a hand area 0.28 m^2.

text: alpha is bounded to the branch up to the first C_L peak (n>0) or trough (n<0) plus one sweep step; V between 1 m/s and Mach 0.6.
note: The upright window edge is pinned through the bound rejection; the inverted window (alpha_peak - step .. 25) is pinned nowhere (P6a-M03 survived) and the bounds handed to opti.variable are not recorded in the stall fakes.

text: The published polar is swept at V_S (the Reynolds number of the stall) with alpha_S among its samples.
note: Fast tier does not notice a polar swept at the bracketing speed (P6a-M14 survived); the aero tier pins it only indirectly through the 1e-6 lift balance.

text: A negative load factor is admissible for the stall (inverted flight) and gives C_L,min on the first trough.
note: Fast tier never calls the adapter with n < 0 (P6a-M16 survived); the aero test asserts signs only.

unit: aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py :: best glide and minimum sink (best_glide_worker, min_sink_worker)
text: Both problems are subject to L = n m g.
note: Fast fakes discard the constraint (Expr.__eq__ returns True unrecorded; P6a-M02 survived); real IPOPT against the closed form pins it to 1e-6.

unit: aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py :: best glide and minimum sink (best_glide_worker, min_sink_worker)
text: A configuration with deflected flaps declares hinge_line_averaged / control_surface_fit_range_unknown on best glide and minimum sink.
note: No test gives best_glide or min_sink a deflected flap; removing the declaration from best_glide survived (P6a-M19).

unit: aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py :: steady roll (OptiAdapter.steady_roll, steady_roll_worker, _roll_window, _roll_start, recording run)
text: The solution satisfies L = m g and the stability-axis rolling moment Cl cos(a) + Cn sin(a) = 0.
note: Fast FakeOpti.subject_to is a no-op: removing the moment constraint (P6a-M04) or dropping g from the lift constraint (P6a-M05) survived; the aero residuals (1e-6 W, 1e-7) pin both.

unit: aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py :: steady roll (OptiAdapter.steady_roll, steady_roll_worker, _roll_window, _roll_start, recording run)
text: For a non-zero command one recording run reports min confidence, max effective alpha (alpha + tau delta) and the per-device confidence; none for a zero command.
note: That the recording run is made at the solved body rates (p cos a, p sin a) is asserted nowhere; P6a-M15 was killed only by an AttributeError of the fake.

unit: aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py :: steady roll (OptiAdapter.steady_roll, steady_roll_worker, _roll_window, _roll_start, recording run)
text: The model key of the roll job holds the aileron command (the rolled airplane is another converted airplane).
note: model_key itself is pinned; that steady_roll passes delta_a_deg into it is not (P6a-M11 survived in the fast tier).

unit: aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py :: steady roll (OptiAdapter.steady_roll, steady_roll_worker, _roll_window, _roll_start, recording run)
text: A missing AeroSandbox is tool_unavailable for steady_roll.
note: steady_roll calls require_available itself; removing the call survived (P6a-M18).

unit: aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py :: steady roll (OptiAdapter.steady_roll, steady_roll_worker, _roll_window, _roll_start, recording run)
text: A non-zero command on an airplane without a roll device is a ValueError (caller defect).
note: P6a-M17 survived.

unit: aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py :: level-flight polar and point (level_polar, level_flight_point, _lift_point, _level_start, _start_at_the_peak)
text: The lift target is n m g; n = 0 is the zero-lift point; n >= 0 finite is admissible.
note: n = 0 is tested on the worker only; the adapter refusing n = 0 survived (P6a-M12).

unit: aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py :: level-flight polar and point (level_polar, level_flight_point, _lift_point, _level_start, _start_at_the_peak)
text: The regime warnings of the polar are those of the slowest and of the fastest point, deduplicated; the drag notice once, last.
note: Both tests give the fastest point a warning-free speed: dropping the fastest point from the check survived (P6a-M06).

unit: aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py :: level-flight polar and point (level_polar, level_flight_point, _lift_point, _level_start, _start_at_the_peak)
text: A level-flight point of a flapped configuration declares the flap caveats.
note: Only level_polar has a flap test (membership of the code); level_flight_point has none.

unit: aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py :: evaluate and sweep entry points, adapter base behaviour
text: sweep refuses every deflected device including a flap (it returns no warnings).
note: Only an aileron is tested; accepting flaps in sweep survived (P6a-M07).

unit: aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py :: evaluate and sweep entry points, adapter base behaviour
text: Every public method raises tool_unavailable when aerosandbox / neuralfoil is missing.
note: steady_roll is not tested (P6a-M18 survived); level_flight_point only through the shared _request.

text: S_ref, b_ref, c_MAC of a known wing equal hand values with the real AeroSandbox.
note: The only real-ASB assert in this package compares the airplane's reference with main_wing_properties, the function that produced it (mirror); hand or ASB-direct values live in test_geometry_properties.py (outside this package).

text: A flap deflection beyond positive_deflection_deg is applied as given; stops are never read or clamped.
note: No test of this package converts a flap whose deflection exceeds its stop; the flap fixtures carry no stops.

text: C_D of the polar is kernel_drag / (q S_ref); one vectorised run with the speed repeated per angle; the flow conditions are recorded.
note: This package's test sets q = 1 and S_ref = 1, so the normalisation is invisible here; test_induced_drag.py (outside) killed P6a-M09.

text: One reynolds_outside_band_at_device (warning) per device with a station below 3e4, with its span share.
note: A device station exactly at 3e4 is not tested (P6a-M08 survived).

text: FixedAtmosphere / the symbolic atmosphere answer density, viscosity, speed of sound and derive T = a^2 / (gamma R), p = rho R T.
note: In this package the two classes are only compared with each other; the formula with literal constants is in test_stall_math.py (outside).

text: Each SECTION line is 'Xle Yle Zle Chord Ainc 1 1' in metres/degrees, followed by AFIL (with x-range on a split piece), the airfoil file and CLAF.
note: The field order of the SECTION line is pinned only by snapshot files the writer itself produced (probe P6b-M05: only the seven snapshot tests fail).

text: A truncated FS or VM table (fewer rows than the mesh has strips) must be an error, never a shorter curve.
note: No test; the fast fixture itself has 3 of 24 strips and 3 shear rows and is accepted by parser and adapter.

text: A station off the devices takes the cut of the nearest controlled station, so the cut is continuous along the span.
note: Only stations inboard of an outboard device are tested, where 'nearest' and 'first controlled' coincide (probe P6b-M04 survived).

text: The ends of a run are stations on every surface: sine-to-tip on the main wing, added breaks on a tail or fin.
note: Pinned for the main wing only; every tail and fin device of the builders spans the whole surface (probe P6b-M02 survived).

text: The horizontal tail takes the main wing's stations inside its span and any other surface the wing's strip width, so the wing's downwash and sidewash act on aligned strips.
note: No test looks at the stations of a tail or fin of the hinge mesh (probe P6b-M03 survived).

text: A station closer than 0.3 strip widths to an added break is dropped.
note: See probe P6b-M12.

text: A fuselage in the run changes the lateral derivatives (destabilising Cn_beta contribution) and is declared.
note: Fast tier pins the BODY block and the notice; the effect on the derivatives is only in the aero tier of another package (test_mvp_chain_real.py).

text: The stations of each side are cosine-spaced in x (bunched at the leading and the trailing edge).
note: See probe P6b-M10.

text: The .avl file carries Sref, Cref, Bref = main_wing_properties s_ref (m^2), c_mac (m), b_ref (m): one authority, and the reference the hinge moment (q S c Chinge), Clp (p b / 2V) and the loads' normalisation rest on.
note: No fast test reads the Sref/Cref/Bref line of a file the adapter wrote (probes P6b-M01, P6b-M07 survived); only the aero tier would notice.

text: neutral_point returns the declared mesh's Xnp (m, geometry frame); it runs 10/24 and the mesh refined by 2 in both counts.
note: The chordwise count of the refined run is checked, the spanwise refinement is not (probe P6b-M20).

text: A held flap splits the main wing at its hinge into front and aft surface, as for the steady roll (Drela's rule 3).
note: Probe P6b-M06: the lateral flap test checks only that a CONTROL line exists.

text: The Reynolds and Mach warnings of ADR 0028 are returned per surface for the given speed and air.
note: Only the presence of reynolds_outside_band at 1 m/s and its absence at 20 m/s; Mach and the device warnings are not exercised here (regime.py is another package).

text: spanwise_loads returns the first surface's rows per q in metres after checking CLtot and that the VM table starts at y = 0; an unmirrored main wing is refused.
note: The adapter test asserts y_strip, c_cl and y_station[0] only; shear and moment and the Bref/Sref the adapter hands to the parser are checked only with real AVL (test_spanwise_loads_real.py, other package). Probe P6b-M19.

text: A body's section at an inserted station is the linear interpolation in x of xyz, a, b, n and n_lower of its neighbours.
note: Every body of the tests has constant a, b, n and centre along x, so the interpolation is never distinguishable from 'take the lower neighbour' (probe P6b-M09).

text: Each half's exponent keeps that half's area: n fits the part above the middle, n_lower the part below.
note: The test asserts the sum of both halves and n != n_lower; swapping the two exponents passes (probe P6b-M08).

text: Each canopy merge reports stations, wetted areas, deviations, clamped exponents and off-centre distance; a target beyond the bracket is clamped and counted.
note: wetted_area_added is only bounded (0 < added < canopy area), clamped_exponents only > 0, perimeter_deviation only < 0.1.

text: Every YAML 1.1 boolean spelling (on/off/yes/no/y/n, any case), as key or value, in an entry or defaults.yaml is a finding with field 'yaml'.
note: taxonomy.yaml is never scanned: 'holds_targets: yes' is silently read as true (observed), and no test covers rules.yaml/config.yaml.

text: An '# ESCALATED:' comment in an entry or defaults.yaml is a finding per comment with its reason; nothing is imported.
note: taxonomy.yaml with an ESCALATED comment imports cleanly (observed); untested and unimplemented.

text: Tabs, a BOM, CRLF line ends, empty values and numbers where strings are expected give a defined outcome (finding or accepted), never a silent wrong value.
note: Empty value and number-as-string are pinned; tab, BOM and CRLF are not (observed: tab -> invalid YAML, BOM -> 'no front matter', CRLF accepted).

text: Dimensional check of law entries (later, report-only).
note: Not in the importer (8.6 says 'later'); done by scripts/check_canon.py, which is tested there.

text: Supplied quantity needs module; final result needs point; intermediate needs stage; derived needs discipline; reference needs module and group.
note: 'an intermediate quantity needs a stage tag' has no negative test; probe P7a-M01 was killed only by the real-canon import.

text: A group's stage and module equal those of its quantity.
note: Only the module disagreement is exercised; dropping the stage comparison survives (P7a-M02).

text: Stage 1 is the formula entry's own 'status'; a formula without one counts as draft.
note: Every test passes a hand-built stage1 dict to derive_approval; the pipeline's reading of 'status:' can be replaced by a constant 'draft' with all tests green (P7a-M15).

text: geometry path, component type/field (or common column), defaults key and app Class.field are looked up in the repository; a missing one is a finding at field 'data'; evaluation and a missing repository are unchecked.
note: Negative cases assert only 'is not None'; through the pipeline only the default kind is exercised.

text: 'consistency:' sources are validated like data sources but do not count for the approval.
note: Only that the real canon carries the field; skipping the location check of consistency sources survives (P7a-M03).

text: Importing the same canon twice yields byte-identical model and report, independent of canon path, file order and hash seed; no date, no path.
note: Both imports run in one process (one hash seed); no test varies PYTHONHASHSEED or the directory order for a successful import. A manual run over 4 seeds gave identical bytes.

text: Each file is written to a temp file next to its target and renamed; a failed first rename leaves the old outputs and no temp file; a failure after the first rename says which file is new; normal permissions.
note: Only os.replace failures are simulated; a failure while writing a temp file (disk full in write, mkstemp error on the second file) is not.

text: Stage 4: the import compares with the committed model, lists added/removed/changed entries and marks breaking changes (inputs, units, outputs, applications) with the affected implementations and golden tests.
note: No diff stage exists in aero_kernel/importer (no 'breaking' anywhere in the package), IMPORT_REPORT.md has no diff section, and no test asks for one.

text: rule_table --check exits 1 when the committed rule_table.json differs from the YAML or is missing; without --check it writes the file.
note: Only the current case (exit 0) is tested; returning 0 on a stale file survives (P7a-M29); the write path is not executed by any test.

text: Every README example equals the front matter of the entry it names (all keys of the example and all machine-readable keys); an unknown entry is a finding.
note: A key of the example outside the fixed machine-readable list (kind, tool) that differs from the entry is never tested (P7a-M20 survived).

text: The run exits 1 on an authoring finding or on a statement finding of any of the four classes, 0 otherwise; the legacy dimensional table is informational.
note: MISMATCH, ADDS_UNLIKE and SCALE are pinned as failing; removing ANGLE from STATEMENT_ERRORS survives (P7a-M19).

text: The legacy per-formula check classifies BALANCES, MISMATCH, SCALE, ADDS_UNLIKE, PROCEDURAL, UNKNOWN_SYMBOL.
note: No fixture gives SCALE (P7a-M21 survived); UNPARSEABLE and UNEVALUABLE are not exercised either.

text: Per formula the implementation file from @formula(slug); per quantity input/done/nonscalar/open; the MVP is the upstream closure of MVP_RESULTS; an implemented formula the canon lacks aborts.
note: Executed by the 'built' fixture, asserted nowhere: swapping done/nonscalar (P7a-M22) and replacing the MVP closure by its seeds (P7a-M26) both survive.

text: An entry's open issues (broken, conflict, missing/partial source unless approved, approximation unless approved, unparseable dimensions) are read from its markers.
note: Inverting the 'unless approved' condition survives (P7a-M25).

text: The page is pure ASCII: \uXXXX in script, CSS escapes in style, numeric references elsewhere.
note: Only build()'s own assert checks 'pure ASCII'; replacing every non-ASCII script character by '?' survives (P7a-M24).

text: Edges per application from the model's bindings (self-edge aborts, model/document mismatch aborts), longest-path layout, default/validation/approval/rule/figure marks, TeX of canonical forms, quantity notes.
note: to_tex, quantity_notes, application_edges, layout, default_marks, validation_rule_marks, approval_marks, rule_marks, figure_marks and binding_constants have no assertion on their output.

text: An interval whose one end sits exactly on an inclusive band edge is inside; on an exclusive edge it is partly.
note: Only Band.position is tested on the edge; no evaluator test puts an interval end on an edge.

text: An interval with min == max is judged like the scalar.
note: Happens incidentally in the end-to-end test (all worlds equal); no dedicated assertion.

text: A NaN value must never be judged inside (Band.position returns INSIDE for NaN).
note: Excluded by the FiniteFloat type of QuantityResult.value and Interval (verified by execution); no test in this package states it, the schema tests are another package.

text: A quantity with status error or skipped is not_available and the text names the status, never not_applicable or inside.
note: No test builds a QuantityResult with status error or skipped; probes M04 and M13 survived.

text: when true lets the rule apply, when false gives not_applicable; when_not likewise; an unevaluable (pending) term gives not_available.
note: A pending term inside when_not is untested (probe M12 survived).

text: The level containing the value is reported; an interval spanning two levels has no level.
note: Only a scalar is tested; the interval-across-levels rule is unpinned (probe M05 survived).

text: Every verdict text names rule, source, quantity, value or interval with worlds, band, severity, meaning and basis.
note: Asserted as exact content for a two-ended band; the band wording of an open band (≥ low, ≤ high) is never asserted (probes M06, M07 survived).

text: RuleVerdict is extra=forbid and frozen.
note: Probe M29 survived.

text: max_inclusive: false puts the upper edge itself outside.
note: Probe M02 survived.

text: A band needs at least one end and min strictly below max.
note: min == max is not tested (probe M10 survived).

text: Band, Level, QuantityRef, Rule and RuleTable reject unknown fields and are frozen, so a mistyped key in the rule YAML is an error.
note: Probe M28 survived: with extra=forbid and frozen removed every test stays green.

text: The shipped bands equal Drela's numbers: SM 0.05-0.15, V_h 0.30-0.60, V_v 0.02-0.05, B > 5, rudder roll authority 0.10-0.20, sideslip <= 15 deg.
note: Asserted as literals (not a mirror) for 7 of 9 rules; the two circling rules over spiral-parameter-mp, every level edge and the caution severity of the aileron circling rule are unpinned (data probes D1-D3 survived).

text: Tail volumes and rudder roll authority above the band are caution with the maintainer's basis; below stays bad; spiral circling with ailerons below is caution.
note: spiral-stability-circling-aileron below_severity caution is not asserted (D1).

text: Worlds exactly with interval uncertainty (>= 2, unique, with a tool in the taxonomy); variables exactly with embeds; closure contains the embeds, sorted and unique.
note: A sorted closure with a duplicate item is not tested (probe M27 survived).

text: A default belongs to a supplied scalar (or catalogue read) of the same unit, > 0 if positive, <= at_most, finite, with basis, source and regime.
note: A default exactly at at_most (admissible) is not tested (probe M21 survived).

text: positive/at_most only on supplied scalars; positive is the boolean true; empty range rejected; abscissa exactly on curves and a scalar; a data source named once and never also in consistency.
note: A source named twice in data or in consistency is not tested (probe M19 survived). Abscissa rules are pinned only by test_importer_abscissa.py (outside this package).

text: A canon validation rule guards exactly one existing input/target quantity or formula; a rule parameter satisfies its own bounds.
note: A rule guarding a derived or output quantity is not tested (probe M20 survived). The parameter bounds are pinned only in test_induced_drag.py, outside this package.

text: A @relation registered for a slug the model lacks is a traceability finding.
note: Registry.slugs() leaves relations out, so check_traceability reports ok (verified by execution); no test.

text: No module under aero_kernel imports app, cad_designer or scripts (Q9), statically and at import.
note: A lazy importlib.import_module('app...') inside a function body is seen by neither the AST scan nor the import-time check.
